fact: A standard professional badminton match is played as the best of three games, with each game played to 21 points using the rally point scoring system.
In badminton, the projectile hit back and forth across the net is called a shuttlecock or birdie, traditionally made with 16 goose feathers.
Badminton officially made its debut as a medal sport at the Summer Olympic Games at Barcelona in 1992.
Lin Dan of China is widely considered one of the greatest badminton players of all time, having won back-to-back Olympic Men's Singles gold medals in 2008 and 2012.
In badminton, the server must hit the shuttlecock below a fixed height of 1.15 meters from the surface of the court.
The Thomas Cup is the premier international men's team championship in badminton, first held in 1948-1949.
Satwiksairaj Rankireddy of India holds the Guinness World Record for the fastest smash in badminton history, recorded at an astonishing 565 km/h (351 mph) in 2023.
The Uber Cup is the premier biennial women's national team badminton championship, named after the British player Betty Uber.
The height of a badminton net is exactly 5 feet and 1 inch (1.55 meters) at the posts and 5 feet (1.524 meters) at the center of the court.
Lee Chong Wei of Malaysia held the World No. 1 ranking for a remarkable 349 weeks during his career, including 199 consecutive weeks from 2008 to 2012.
If the score reaches 20-all in badminton, the side that gains a 2-point lead first wins the game, up to a maximum cap of 30 points (where 30-29 wins).
Prakash Padukone became the first Indian to win the prestigious All England Open Badminton Championship in 1980, defeating Liem Swie King in London.
The modern game of badminton was developed in the 19th century in British India, originally known as 'Poona' before being popularized at the Duke of Beaufort's Badminton House in Gloucestershire.
Pearly Tan of Malaysia holds the Guinness World Record for the fastest smash by a female badminton player, clocked at 438 km/h (272 mph).

The longest recorded rally in competitive badminton history lasted 211 shots (3 minutes and 50 seconds) between Pearly Tan / Thinaah Muralitharan and Rena Miyaura / Ayako Sakuramoto at the 2023 Malaysia Masters.
An official competitive feather shuttlecock must weigh between 4.74 and 5.50 grams and have a skirt diameter of 58 to 68 millimeters.
Indonesia is the most successful nation in Thomas Cup history, having won the men's team world championship 14 times.
Viktor Axelsen of Denmark set a modern record in 2022 by winning 39 consecutive international matches and claiming 8 individual titles in a single season.
